reference/opengl.text: opengl import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/opengl" Functions Function func Wake() Wake makes a window that draws on demand draw a frame now: for a program whose data changes on another goroutine (a download finishing, a message arriving). Constants and variables var ( // FramebufferIncomplete is a framebuffer OpenGL cannot draw into, such as the shadow map's on // a driver that lacks depth textures. Its details give OpenGL's status. FramebufferIncomplete = failure.Define("opengl.framebuffer-incomplete", "OpenGL cannot draw into the framebuffer") // WindowNotOpened is a window GLFW could not open: no display, or no OpenGL 4.1. WindowNotOpened = failure.Define("opengl.window-not-opened", "the window could not be opened") // ContextNotStarted is OpenGL's functions failing to load in the window's context. ContextNotStarted = failure.Define("opengl.context-not-started", "OpenGL could not start") // ShaderNotCompiled is a shader the driver would not compile. Its details give the driver's log. ShaderNotCompiled = failure.Define("opengl.shader-not-compiled", "OpenGL could not compile a shader") // ProgramNotLinked is two shaders the driver would not link. Its details give the driver's log. ProgramNotLinked = failure.Define("opengl.program-not-linked", "OpenGL could not link a shader program") // FrameNotSaved is a captured frame that could not be written to its file. FrameNotSaved = failure.Define("opengl.frame-not-saved", "the frame could not be saved") // NotImplemented is an immediate-mode shape the OpenGL renderer cannot draw yet. NotImplemented = failure.Define("opengl.not-implemented", "the OpenGL renderer cannot draw this shape yet") ) Codes of the errors the OpenGL backend returns. Area Area is a rectangle of the framebuffer, in its pixels, from its bottom-left corner as OpenGL counts. type Area struct{ X, Y, Width, Height int } FlatRenderer FlatRenderer draws a 2D draw list on a plain background, with no scene, sky or camera: the window of an application that is only an interface. It uses the overlay's atlas and shaders, so a whole frame is one clear and one draw call. Create and use it on the thread that owns the OpenGL context. type FlatRenderer struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func NewFlatRenderer(fonts overlay.Fonts) (*FlatRenderer, error) NewFlatRenderer prepares the atlas and shaders; text is drawn in fonts (overlay.Fonts{} for the default ones). func (renderer *FlatRenderer) Draw(list *draw2d.List, background draw2d.Color, width, height int, scale float32) Draw clears the framebuffer (width × height pixels) to the background colour and paints the list. FrameStatistics FrameStatistics describes the last frame drawn (see sceneplan.FrameStatistics). type FrameStatistics = sceneplan.FrameStatistics PassTimes PassTimes are GPU durations of the passes of one frame. type PassTimes = sceneplan.PassTimes Renderer Renderer draws immediate-mode shapes (immediate.Renderer) with OpenGL, in the window's current program. Its zero value is ready; it makes its buffers on the first shape and reuses them, so a shape allocates nothing on the Go side. type Renderer struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func (renderer *Renderer) RenderImage(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, bytes []byte, centre graphics.Vector, width float32, height float32, shader *string) error RenderImage returns NotImplemented: OpenGL cannot draw pictures in immediate mode yet. func (renderer *Renderer) RenderModel(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, model *immediate.Model, shader *string) error RenderModel draws every mesh of the model. func (renderer *Renderer) RenderObject(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, vertices []graphics.Vector, shader *string) error RenderObject draws the triangles of a 3D object, three vertices each. func (renderer *Renderer) RenderPolygon(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, coordinates []graphics.Vector, shader *string, fill bool) error RenderPolygon returns NotImplemented: OpenGL cannot draw polygons yet. func (renderer *Renderer) RenderRectangle(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, centre graphics.Vector, width float32, height float32, shader *string, fill bool) error RenderRectangle draws a rectangle of width × height centred on centre, in the plane z = centre's z. func (renderer *Renderer) RenderTriangle(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, coordinates []graphics.Vector, shader *string, fill bool) error RenderTriangle draws triangles, three coordinates each. func (renderer *Renderer) SetMatrices(projection, view, model graphics.Matrix) SetMatrices sets the matrices the next shapes are drawn with. SceneRenderer SceneRenderer draws a scene.Scene. Meshes and instances are uploaded once and kept on the GPU; they are uploaded again only when marked Dirty (for simulations). It must be created and used on the thread that owns the OpenGL context. type SceneRenderer struct { Shadows ShadowSettings Profiling bool // measure CPU and GPU times into Statistics (waits for the GPU every frame) Statistics FrameStatistics // the last frame drawn // OverlayScale is how many framebuffer pixels make one pixel of the overlay (labels, header, // notices): 2 on a high-density screen, so they keep their size; 0 = 1. OverlayScale float32 // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func NewSceneRenderer(fonts overlay.Fonts) (*SceneRenderer, error) NewSceneRenderer compiles the scene shaders; the overlay's text is drawn in fonts (overlay.Fonts{} for the default ones). func (renderer *SceneRenderer) Draw(world *scene.Scene, camera camera.Lens, width, height int, seconds float64) Draw renders the scene from the camera into the current framebuffer of the given size, then its overlay on top. func (renderer *SceneRenderer) DrawIn(world *scene.Scene, camera camera.Lens, area Area, seconds float64) DrawIn renders the scene from the camera into an area of the current framebuffer, clearing only that area, and without the scene's overlay: several scenes can share a frame (a preview of a console's two screens), and an overlay over all of them is drawn once after (DrawOverlay). func (renderer *SceneRenderer) DrawOver(world *scene.Scene, camera camera.Lens, area Area, seconds float64) DrawOver renders the scene from the camera into an area over what the framebuffer holds there: it clears only the depth and draws no sky, so the scene floats over the one behind it (a radar in a corner of a game's view). func (renderer *SceneRenderer) DrawOverlay(world *scene.Scene, width, height int) DrawOverlay draws a scene's overlay (its labels, notices and drawing) over the whole framebuffer, with the camera of the last DrawIn. ShadowSettings ShadowSettings controls the sun shadows (see sceneplan.ShadowSettings). type ShadowSettings = sceneplan.ShadowSettings Function or method func DefaultShadowSettings() ShadowSettings DefaultShadowSettings returns enabled shadows with automatic sizes. Window Window runs a window.Application in an OpenGL 4.1 window. Its zero value is ready to use. type Window struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func (opengl *Window) Draw(app *window.Application) error Draw draws a frame: the immediate-mode matrices from the application's camera, a clear to its background, then its Draw callback. func (opengl *Window) Run(app *window.Application) error Run opens the window and runs the application until it closes or sets Stop; a Headless application draws one frame into a hidden window and saves it. func (opengl *Window) SaveFrame(app *window.Application, path string) error SaveFrame saves the frame just drawn (and not yet shown) as a PNG at path. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/opengl-overlay.title: opengl/overlay
reference/opengl-overlay.text: opengl/overlay import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/opengl/overlay" Package overlay lays out the scene's overlay (labels over the world, the header and the notices, see scene.Overlay) as textured rectangles in screen pixels, ready for a backend to draw with one texture: the Atlas, which holds the glyphs of the text, the Lucide icons and the corners of the rounded pills. It does no drawing itself and needs no graphics context, so it can be tested anywhere; the OpenGL scene renderer uploads its atlas and draws its quads. Functions Function func DefaultFontFolders() []string DefaultFontFolders are where the system's fonts are looked for by default, for characters the program's fonts lack: Android's own, or the usual folders of the desktop's system. Constants and variables var FontNotRead = failure.Define("overlay.font-not-read", "a font could not be read") FontNotRead is returned by NewPainter and NewMeasurer when one of the fonts (the default ones or those given in Fonts) is not a TrueType or OpenType font. Atlas Atlas is one grey image holding everything the overlay draws: the glyphs of the text, the icons and the rounded corners of the pills. Every picture is a coverage mask (0 = empty, 255 = covered) that the backend tints when it draws it, so a single texture and a single draw call paint the whole overlay. Pictures are added when first needed and never move; when the image is full it doubles in size (keeping what it had in the same place). Version changes whenever pixels change, so the backend knows to upload the image again. type Atlas struct { Image *image.Alpha Version int // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func NewAtlas() *Atlas NewAtlas returns an empty atlas. func (atlas *Atlas) Size() int Size returns the side of the square image, in pixels. Entry Entry is a picture in the atlas: where its pixels are, and where to draw them relative to a pen position (for glyphs, the dot on the baseline). type Entry struct { Bounds image.Rectangle // pixels in the atlas Offset image.Point // top-left corner of the picture relative to the pen Advance float32 // how far the pen moves after a glyph, in pixels } Fonts Fonts are what a Painter or a Measurer draws text with: the TrueType or OpenType fonts, one per weight, and where the system's fonts are, for the characters they lack. The zero value is the default: the Go fonts and the system's usual folders. type Fonts struct { // Regular, Medium, Bold and Mono are a font file's bytes each; an empty one keeps the Go font // of that weight. Regular, Medium, Bold, Mono []byte // Folders are where the system's fonts and colour emoji are looked for, for characters the // fonts lack. nil is DefaultFontFolders(); an empty, non-nil list looks nowhere, and such // characters are drawn as a question mark. Folders []string } Frame Frame is what the layout needs to know about the frame being drawn. type Frame struct { ViewProjection graphics.Matrix // the camera's projection times its view Width, Height int // framebuffer size in pixels Scale float32 // framebuffer pixels per layout pixel: 2 on a high-density screen; 0 = 1 VerticalScale float32 // the scene's vertical exaggeration; 0 = 1 } LightQuad LightQuad is a light laid out: a square of the screen it shines on, its colour (alpha: its intensity) and either a picture it shines through (Pictured), or a disc that is full inside Inner (a share of the square's half side) and fades to nothing at its edge. type LightQuad struct { Screen [4]float32 // left, top, right, bottom on screen Color [4]float32 Picture [4]float32 // where it reads its picture in the Pictures, when Pictured Pictured bool Inner float32 } Lighting Lighting asks the backend, before it draws the quad at At, to light everything drawn so far: the lights from First to Last (in Lights) are added over Ambient into a picture of light, which then multiplies what is on screen. Light is kept at half (0.5 leaves a colour as it is), so it can brighten up to twice. type Lighting struct { At, First, Last int Ambient [4]float32 // Area is what it lights on screen (left, top, right, bottom): its list's clip, or the whole // frame. Area [4]float32 } Measurer Measurer measures text the way the painter draws it, without an atlas or a graphics context, so an interface library can lay out its controls before the frame is drawn. It implements draw2d.Measurer. type Measurer struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func NewMeasurer(chosen Fonts) (*Measurer, error) NewMeasurer reads the fonts (Fonts{} for the default ones). func (measurer *Measurer) HasIcon(name string) bool HasIcon tells whether Lucide has an icon of this name. func (measurer *Measurer) MeasureText(text string, size float32, weight draw2d.Weight, scale float32) draw2d.TextMetrics MeasureText measures a line at a size in layout pixels on a screen of a density (see draw2d.Measurer). Painter Painter lays out overlays frame after frame, keeping the atlas and the fonts between frames. It is used from one goroutine, the one that draws. type Painter struct { // Warn hears of a problem once (an unknown icon name, lights a GPU cannot draw); nil = the // default slog logger, which the program sets with slog.SetDefault (on the Nintendo 3DS, a line // on the console). Warn func(message string) // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func NewPainter(chosen Fonts) (*Painter, error) NewPainter reads the fonts (Fonts{} for the default ones) and prepares an empty atlas. func (painter *Painter) Atlas() *Atlas Atlas returns the image the quads point into. func (painter *Painter) Lightings() []Lighting Lightings list where, in the quads Paint just gave, the backend lights what it drew so far; empty when nothing is lit, which then costs nothing. func (painter *Painter) Lights() []LightQuad Lights are the lights Paint laid out, which the Lightings take in turn. func (painter *Painter) Paint(overlay *scene.Overlay, anchors map[*scene.Node]graphics.Matrix, frame Frame) []Quad Paint lays out the whole overlay for a frame. func (painter *Painter) Pictures() *Pictures Pictures returns the image pictured quads read their colours from. func (painter *Painter) Report(message string) Report tells the program of a problem a frame works around: through Warn when the program set it, otherwise through warnByDefault (the default slog logger; a line on the console on the Nintendo 3DS, where slog would cost about 42 KB of every program). func (painter *Painter) Snapshots() []Snapshot Snapshots lists where, in the quads Paint just gave, the backend takes and blurs a picture of the frame so far; empty when nothing on screen is frosted, which then costs nothing. Pictures Pictures is the second atlas: the colours of the images a draw list shows (photos, a video's frames), side by side in one RGBA image. A picture's quads read their colours here and their coverage (the rounded corners) in the grey Atlas, so images are drawn in the same single draw call as everything else. A picture is copied in the first time it is drawn, and copied again into the same place when it changes (draw2d.Image.Changed). When no room is left, the image grows; at its largest, it is emptied and holds only the pictures of the frame being drawn. A backend uploads what changed: the whole image after it grew or was emptied, else only the areas pictures were copied into. The image is made with the first picture: an interface without any needs none. type Pictures struct { Image *image.NRGBA // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func NewPictures() *Pictures NewPictures returns an empty picture atlas, with no image yet. func (pictures *Pictures) Pending() (whole bool, areas []image.Rectangle) Pending tells what to upload: the whole image, or only some areas of it (none when nothing changed). func (pictures *Pictures) Size() int Size returns the side of the square image, in pixels: 0 before the first picture. func (pictures *Pictures) Uploaded() Uploaded forgets what Pending told. Projection Projection is where a point of the world falls on screen. type Projection struct { X, Y float32 // pixels from the top-left corner Depth float32 // -1 at the near plane, 1 at the far plane: smaller is nearer Visible bool // in front of the camera and inside the screen } Function or method func Project(point graphics.Vector, frame Frame) Projection Project places a world point on screen, applying the vertical exaggeration as the scene shaders do. Quad Quad is a rectangle of the atlas drawn on screen with a colour: the atlas gives the coverage, the colour the paint. A quad of an image also reads its colours in the Pictures, which the colour then tints. Coordinates are pixels, with the origin at the top-left corner. type Quad struct { Screen [4]float32 // left, top, right, bottom on screen Atlas [4]float32 // left, top, right, bottom in the atlas Color [4]float32 // straight RGBA; its alpha multiplies the coverage // Picture is where the quad reads its colours in the Pictures (left, top, right, bottom), when // Pictured. Picture [4]float32 Pictured bool Sharp bool // the picture is read at the nearest pixel (draw2d.Image's Sharp) // Backdrop quads show the blurred picture of what was drawn before them (see Snapshot), cut // by the atlas's coverage, instead of their colour. Backdrop bool } Snapshot Snapshot asks the backend, before it draws the quad at At, to take a picture of everything drawn so far and blur it by Blur screen pixels (a standard deviation): the backdrop quads after it read that picture. There is one per layer that has backdrops, so many glass panels cost one blur. type Snapshot struct { At int Blur float32 } ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/packages.title: Reference
reference/packages.text: Reference Every public package, type and function, with the first sentence of its documentation. The pages are generated from the doc comments ( python3 docs/5-reference/generate.py from the repository's root), so they say exactly what go doc says; for the whole comment of anything, run go doc github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene.Mesh or open the source. Which package do I need? I want to… Package Show a scene in a window, with cameras, a sun and captures viewer Describe a scene: nodes, meshes, materials, instances, sky, water, labels scene Open a .glb or .gltf loaders Read the keyboard, the mouse and fingers input Move a camera myself, or find what is under the pointer camera Paint flat shapes, text, icons and pictures over the view draw2d Vectors, matrices, transforms graphics A made-up island to test with scene/sample Run my own program in a window: its options, update and draw window Draw triangles myself every frame (immediate mode) immediate Core Package What it is scene The retained scene: nodes, meshes, materials, instances, levels of detail, the environment (sun, sky, fog, water, wind, snow) and the overlay (labels, header, notices, a free drawing) viewer The interactive explorer: Run for programs that animate, Edit for programs that change the scene in answer to the person; options and flags input A snapshot of the keyboard, mouse and touch screen at each step; claims, the clipboard, the pointer's shape, frames asked for camera The Camera ; orbit, walking and map controllers; the ray through a pixel draw2d A list of flat shapes in layout pixels, which the backends paint over everything loaders glTF 2.0 with the renderer's extras graphics Vector , Matrix , transformations and projections window A program in a window: its Options , its Callbacks (update, draw) and the Application they make immediate The immediate-mode Renderer contract: shapes drawn at once, every frame scene/sample A made-up island that uses every feature, needing no files failure Error codes: Define , Wrap , checked with errors.Is Platforms and internals Programs rarely use these directly: viewer and go-ui's window choose and drive them. Package What it is opengl The OpenGL 4.1 backend: the window, the scene renderer, the flat renderer opengl/overlay Lays the overlay out as quads of one atlas: fonts, icons, the text measurer metal Metal on macOS: flat and scene windows and renderers gles Renderers written once for OpenGL ES: WebGL2 in browsers, Android browser A canvas as the window, built with GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm android The program as a NativeActivity: window, touches, keyboard, screen reader, built with GOOS=android windowloop The GLFW window loop OpenGL and Metal share frameloop The fixed-step clock every loop shares software , vulkan , webgpu Backends of the immediate-mode contract, to be built later: every function returns <backend>.not-implemented The backends also share two packages of the module's own, which programs cannot import: internal/sceneplan (what a frame of a scene draws, worked out once for every backend) and internal/shading (what every backend's shaders agree on). Conventions These hold across every package. Topic Rule Axes y is up; the ground is the x–z plane; north is −z Units The scene's units are yours (metres, kilometres); some defaults scale with the scene's size Points and directions A Vector with 1 last is a point, with 0 a direction; colours use it as opacity Matrices Column-major, as OpenGL; a.Multiply(b) applies b first; translation in elements 12, 13, 14 Scene colours Linear RGB(A), 0 to 1, lit and gamma-corrected by the renderer Screen colours draw2d.Color and the overlay's tints are as seen on screen, not gamma-corrected Screen positions draw2d and touches: layout pixels from the top-left corner, multiplied by the screen's density when drawn. input.State.CursorX / CursorY and viewer.View : window pixels Time Update functions run at a fixed step (1/60 s by default), whatever the frame rate Goroutines Update and edit functions run on the drawing goroutine: change the scene there, with no locks. From another goroutine, wake the window ( opengl.Wake ) and hand the change over Uploads Meshes and instances are uploaded once; set Dirty (or Instances.MarkChanged ) after changing them Zero values A zero field usually means "the default" ( FogFar 0 = no fog, VerticalScale 0 = 1); the field's comment says which Icons By Lucide name, everywhere ← Documentation

reference/scene.title: scene
reference/scene.text: scene import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene" Package scene is a retained, backend-independent description of a 3D scene: nodes with transforms, meshes with per-vertex normals and colors, materials, GPU instancing and the environment (sun, sky, fog, water). Backends upload meshes once and draw them every frame. Simulations can change geometry or instances later and mark them Dirty so the backend uploads them again. Constants and variables const DefaultMaximumNotices = 5 DefaultMaximumNotices is how many notices are shown at once when the overlay does not say. const DefaultNoticeSeconds = 6.0 DefaultNoticeSeconds is how long a notice stays, in seconds, when the overlay does not say. Clouds Clouds is a procedural cloud layer. type Clouds struct { Coverage float32 // share of the sky covered (0 = clear) Color graphics.Vector Speed float32 // drift in cloud-texture units per second Scale float32 // size of the cloud pattern (larger = bigger clouds) Offset graphics.Vector // how far the clouds have drifted (x, z), moved by a simulation } Constellation Constellation is a figure of stars joined by lines, fixed to the night sky. type Constellation struct { Name string Stars []graphics.Vector // directions as seen at midnight (the sun at the lowest point of its circle) Lines [][2]int // pairs of indices into Stars Color graphics.Vector } Daylight Daylight is the state of the sky at the current sun height: the colors to paint and the single directional light (sun or moon) that lights and shadows the scene. Backends compute it once per frame with Environment.Daylight. type Daylight struct { DayAmount float32 // 1 in full day, 0 at night TwilightAmount float32 // 1 with the sun on the horizon, 0 far from it Zenith graphics.Vector Horizon graphics.Vector Fog graphics.Vector SkyLight graphics.Vector // ambient light from the sky GroundLight graphics.Vector // ambient light bounced from the ground SunVisible float32 // how much of the sun disc is above the horizon LightDirection graphics.Vector // towards the light that shades the scene LightColor graphics.Vector MoonDirection graphics.Vector StarRotation graphics.Matrix // turns world directions into celestial directions Brightness float32 // overall light level (1 day, low at night) for materials that are not lit } DetailLevel DetailLevel is a simpler version of a mesh. It replaces the finer versions when the model looks smaller on screen than ScreenSize, a fraction of the screen height (0.05 = a twentieth of it). type DetailLevel struct { Mesh *Mesh ScreenSize float32 } Environment Environment holds the lighting and atmosphere. type Environment struct { SunDirection graphics.Vector // towards the sun, normalized SunColor graphics.Vector SkyZenith graphics.Vector SkyHorizon graphics.Vector GroundAmbient graphics.Vector Ambient float32 FogColor graphics.Vector FogNear float32 FogFar float32 // 0 = no fog Water *Water VerticalScale float32 // vertical exaggeration applied to the whole scene (0 = 1) Sky *Sky // sky over the day and night (nil = DefaultSky) Wind Wind Snow *Snow // snow on the ground above a height (nil = none) FoliageTint graphics.Vector // colour foliage materials take (alpha = how much; zero = none): the season's } Function or method func DefaultEnvironment() Environment DefaultEnvironment returns a daylight environment. func (environment Environment) Daylight() Daylight Daylight computes the sky and the lighting for the current sun direction. func (environment Environment) EffectiveSky() *Sky EffectiveSky returns the sky, or the default sky when unset. func (environment Environment) EffectiveVerticalScale() float32 EffectiveVerticalScale returns the vertical scale, treating 0 as 1. HeaderLine HeaderLine is one line of the header in the top-left corner of the screen. type HeaderLine struct { Icon string Text string Tint graphics.Vector // colour of the icon (alpha 0 = the default text colour) } Instances Instances draws a mesh many times with a transform and a color per instance. After changing instances, a simulation either sets Dirty (instances were added or removed, or most of them changed: everything is prepared again) or lists the changed ones with MarkChanged (only those are uploaded). The backend clears both. type Instances struct { Transforms []graphics.Matrix Colors []graphics.Vector Dirty bool Changed []int // indices changed since the last draw GPU any } Function or method func (instances *Instances) MarkChanged(indices ...int) MarkChanged records that these instances changed their transform or color. Label Label is a small tag drawn above something in the world: an icon, a text and an optional badge under them. It keeps the same size on screen however far the camera is. type Label struct { // Node anchors the label to a node: it follows the node's world transform and hides with it. // When nil, the label stands at Point. Node *Node Point graphics.Vector // world position of the anchor when there is no Node // Height lifts the label above its anchor, in world units (the top of a box, for example). Height float32 Text string Icon string // name of a Lucide icon (https://lucide.dev), drawn before the text or alone Badge string // a short text in a small pill under the label // Tint colours the icon and the badge, as a screen colour (see draw2d.ParseHex); alpha 0 = the // default text colour. The text itself stays dark on a light pill, so it always reads well. Tint graphics.Vector Hidden bool } Function or method func (label *Label) IsEmpty() bool IsEmpty tells whether the label has nothing to draw. LevelVariation LevelVariation raises and lowers a water surface with one harmonic that differs from place to place: at each point the offset is InPhase·cos(Angle) + InQuadrature·sin(Angle), which is Amplitude·cos(Angle − Phase) with InPhase = Amplitude·cos(Phase) and InQuadrature = Amplitude·sin(Phase). A simulation moves Angle (tides advance it a full turn per period); the grids stay the same. Outside the area the values of the nearest edge apply. type LevelVariation struct { MinimumX, MinimumZ float32 // corner of the area (world units) MaximumX, MaximumZ float32 // opposite corner; grid values sit at cell centres Columns, Rows int InPhase []float32 // Rows×Columns, row by row from MinimumZ; heights in world units InQuadrature []float32 Angle float32 // radians Dirty bool // the grids changed: backends upload them again GPU any } Function or method func (variation *LevelVariation) OffsetAt(x, z float32) float32 OffsetAt returns the height of the surface above the water level at a point. Material Material describes how a mesh is shaded. type Material struct { Name string Kind MaterialKind BaseColor graphics.Vector // linear RGBA multiplied with vertex colors DoubleSided bool Transparent bool // Additive adds the surface's light to what is behind it instead of covering it: beams, sparks, // glows. It never darkens, and is drawn with the transparent surfaces (its alpha scales it). Additive bool Sway float32 // how much the wind bends the mesh (0 = rigid); for plants modelled with height 1 DepthBias float32 // pulls the surface towards the camera by this share of its distance, so thin surfaces // lying on terrain (rivers, roads) stay visible over the terrain's simpler far versions; 0 = none Pattern Pattern // procedural surface pattern of lit and glowing materials PatternScale float32 // size of one pattern cell (a stone, a course, a shingle) in world units Foliage bool // takes the environment's FoliageTint (leaves that change with the seasons) } MaterialKind MaterialKind selects the shading model. type MaterialKind int const ( LitKind MaterialKind = iota // diffuse sun + sky ambient + fog UnlitKind // flat color (+ fog) WaterKind // animated water surface WaterfallKind // animated, translucent falling water GlowKind // lit by day; shines with its own colour in the dark (glowing flowers, lamps) ) Mesh Mesh is triangle geometry. Positions and normals are xyz triples, colors rgba quads (linear). Indices are optional: without them every three vertices form a triangle. type Mesh struct { Name string Positions []float32 Normals []float32 Colors []float32 Indices []uint32 Material *Material Details []DetailLevel // simpler versions for when the mesh looks small, from finer to coarser Ground bool // walkable surface (used by GroundHeight) Dirty bool // geometry changed: backends upload it again GPU any // backend handle } Function or method func (mesh *Mesh) Bounds() (minimum, maximum graphics.Vector) Bounds returns the box around the mesh positions in its own coordinates. func (mesh *Mesh) ComputeNormals() ComputeNormals fills smooth vertex normals from the triangles (weighted by triangle area). func (mesh *Mesh) ForEachTriangle(visit func(first, second, third uint32)) ForEachTriangle calls visit with the vertex indices of every triangle. func (mesh *Mesh) Level(index int) *Mesh Level returns a version of the mesh: 0 is the mesh itself, 1 the first detail level, and so on. func (mesh *Mesh) LevelCount() int LevelCount returns how many versions the mesh has, itself included. func (mesh *Mesh) LevelForScreenSize(screenSize float32) int LevelForScreenSize returns the index of the version to draw for a model of this apparent size: the coarsest level whose ScreenSize is still larger than it. func (mesh *Mesh) Top() float32 Top returns the highest y of the mesh's vertices (0 for an empty mesh), to lift a label above it. func (mesh *Mesh) Vertex(index uint32) graphics.Vector Vertex returns the position of a vertex. func (mesh *Mesh) VertexCount() int VertexCount returns the number of vertices. Moon Moon is a disc with phases that also lights the scene at night. type Moon struct { Direction graphics.Vector // towards the moon; zero = opposite the sun AngularSize float32 // apparent diameter in radians Color graphics.Vector Phase float32 // 0 new, 0.25 first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 last quarter LightIntensity float32 // moonlight on the scene at full moon, relative to the sun } Node Node places a mesh (optionally instanced) in the world; children inherit the transform. type Node struct { Name string Transform graphics.Matrix Mesh *Mesh Instances *Instances Children []*Node Hidden bool // Moving says the node's transform changes often, turning as well as moving: a ship, a // vehicle. Backends that work a mesh's light out once for each way it is turned (nintendo3ds, on the // 3DS) light a moving node on the GPU every frame instead. Moving bool Tags map[string]any // free data from the file (glTF extras) for the application } Notice Notice is a short message shown under the header for a few seconds, newest first. type Notice struct { Icon string Text string Tint graphics.Vector // colour of the icon (alpha 0 = the default text colour) Added float64 // the overlay's Clock when the notice was added } Overlay Overlay is what is drawn over the 3D view, in screen space: labels that float above things in the world, a header pinned to the top-left corner and short notices under it, and a free drawing on top of everything (Drawing). The overlay itself handles no input: an interface library fills Drawing with its panels and buttons and reads the mouse and keyboard on its own. A program changes it from the viewer's update function, which runs on the same goroutine as the drawing, so no locking is needed. The zero value is an empty overlay ready to use. type Overlay struct { Labels []*Label Header []HeaderLine Notices []Notice // Drawing is drawn last, over the labels, header and notices: flat shapes, text and icons in // screen space, filled every frame by a program or an interface library. nil = nothing. Drawing *draw2d.List // Clock counts the seconds the overlay has been shown; the viewer advances it at every step. // Notices remember the clock reading when they were added, so they fade on the viewer's time. Clock float64 // NoticeDuration is how long a notice stays, in seconds, fading at the end; 0 = DefaultNoticeSeconds. NoticeDuration float64 // MaximumNotices is how many notices are shown at once, the newest; 0 = DefaultMaximumNotices. MaximumNotices int } Function or method func (overlay *Overlay) AddLabel(label *Label) AddLabel shows a label; the caller keeps the pointer to change or remove it later. func (overlay *Overlay) AddNotice(icon, text string, tint graphics.Vector) AddNotice shows a message now; it fades after the notice duration. func (overlay *Overlay) Advance(seconds float64) Advance moves the overlay's clock on and forgets the notices that have faded out. func (overlay *Overlay) IsEmpty() bool IsEmpty tells whether there is nothing to draw on the overlay. func (overlay *Overlay) RemoveLabel(label *Label) RemoveLabel stops showing a label. func (overlay *Overlay) VisibleNotices() []VisibleNotice VisibleNotices returns the notices to draw now, newest first, at most MaximumNotices. Pattern Pattern is a procedural surface pattern that modulates a lit material's colour, computed from the world position (no texture): stones, blocks, shingles… It fades out where its cells get too small on screen. type Pattern int const ( PatternNone Pattern = iota PatternCobbles // irregular paving stones with joints (horizontal surfaces) PatternMasonry // courses of stone blocks with mortar (walls) PatternPlaster // mottled render PatternShingles // overlapping rows of shingles or slates (roofs) PatternPlanks // wooden planks PatternGrass // mottled grass ) The patterns; PatternNone leaves the material's colour as it is. Function or method func PatternNamed(name string) Pattern PatternNamed returns the pattern with a name (cobbles, masonry, plaster, shingles, planks, grass); PatternNone for any other name. PointLight PointLight is a light that shines from a point all around, as a lamp: full within Inner of it and fading smoothly to nothing at Outer (world units), the same fade as draw2d's point lights. It lights the lit materials it reaches, besides the sun and the sky; each draw takes the few that reach it (see sceneplan.MaxLightsPerDraw). type PointLight struct { Position graphics.Vector // in the world, before the vertical scale // Color is linear, like the materials'; its alpha is the intensity (1 a plain lamp, up to a few). Color graphics.Vector Inner, Outer float32 } Scene Scene is the root of a scene. type Scene struct { Nodes []*Node Environment Environment Tags map[string]any Overlay Overlay // labels, header and notices drawn over the view // Lights are the point lights besides the sun; a program changes them between frames as its // lamps move. Lights []PointLight // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func New() *Scene New returns an empty scene with the default environment. func (scene *Scene) Bounds() (minimum, maximum graphics.Vector) Bounds returns the world-space bounding box of all meshes (instances counted by their origin). func (scene *Scene) GroundHeight(x, z float32) (float32, bool) GroundHeight returns the highest walkable surface at (x, z), before vertical scaling. func (scene *Scene) InvalidateGround() InvalidateGround drops the ground index; call it after changing walkable meshes. func (scene *Scene) Walk(visit func(node *Node, world graphics.Matrix)) Walk visits every visible node with its world transform. func (scene *Scene) WorldTransforms(wanted map[*Node]bool) map[*Node]graphics.Matrix WorldTransforms returns the world transform of every visible node, for anchoring labels. Sky Sky describes what is drawn behind the scene over a whole day and how it lights the scene at night. The height of the sun decides the time of day: above the horizon it is day, near it twilight, below it night. By default the sky is procedural: the day gradient of the environment, a twilight glow, and a night with stars, a moon and constellations; clouds float over both. Images can replace the day or the night (a skybox): an equirectangular panorama or six cube faces. type Sky struct { NightZenith graphics.Vector // sky color straight up at night (linear) NightHorizon graphics.Vector // sky color at the horizon at night NightAmbient graphics.Vector // sky light that reaches the scene at night TwilightColor graphics.Vector // horizon glow at dawn and dusk CelestialPole graphics.Vector // axis the night sky turns around (towards the visible pole) Stars Stars Moon *Moon // nil = no moon Clouds Clouds Constellations []Constellation DayImage *SkyImage // replaces the procedural day sky NightImage *SkyImage // replaces the procedural night sky; it turns with the stars } Function or method func DefaultSky() *Sky DefaultSky returns an Earth-like sky: stars, a full moon opposite the sun and no clouds. SkyImage SkyImage is a skybox: an equirectangular panorama or six cube faces (+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z). type SkyImage struct { Equirectangular image.Image Faces [6]image.Image GPU any // backend handle } Function or method func (skyImage *SkyImage) IsCube() bool IsCube reports whether the image is made of six faces. Snow Snow covers the lit surfaces that face up above a height, blending over a band. type Snow struct { Level float32 // world units, before vertical scaling Blend float32 // world units over which the snow fades in Color graphics.Vector // linear } Stars Stars is a procedural star field. type Stars struct { Density float32 // share of the sky cells that hold a star (0 = no stars, 1 = one per cell) Brightness float32 // brightness multiplier Twinkle float32 // amount of twinkling (0 = steady) DaytimeVisibility float32 // how visible the stars stay in full daylight (0 = only at night) } VisibleNotice VisibleNotice is a notice as it should be drawn now. type VisibleNotice struct { Notice Opacity float32 // 1 while fresh, falling to 0 as the notice ends } Water Water is an infinite animated water plane. type Water struct { Level float32 Shallow graphics.Vector Deep graphics.Vector Size float32 // extent of the plane (world units) WaveLength float32 // length of the main wave (world units); 0 = Size / 2000 FloorDepth float32 // depth of an opaque floor drawn under the water; 0 = Size / 500 ColorDepth float32 // water depth at which the color is about two thirds of the way from Shallow to Deep; 0 = FloorDepth / 8 Variation *LevelVariation // raises and lowers the surface over an area (tides, for example); nil = flat ShoreFade float32 // depth over which the sea fades into the shore; 0 = ColorDepth / 20 } Function or method func (water *Water) EffectiveColorDepth() float32 EffectiveColorDepth returns the color depth, deriving it from the floor depth when unset. func (water *Water) EffectiveFloorDepth() float32 EffectiveFloorDepth returns the floor depth, deriving it from the size when unset. func (water *Water) EffectiveShoreFade() float32 EffectiveShoreFade returns the shore fade depth, deriving it from the color depth when unset. func (water *Water) EffectiveWaveLength() float32 EffectiveWaveLength returns the wave length, deriving it from the size when unset. func (water *Water) LevelAt(x, z float32) float32 LevelAt returns the height of the water surface at a point. Wind Wind moves clouds and bends plants (materials with Sway). type Wind struct { Direction graphics.Vector // horizontal direction the wind blows towards Strength float32 // 0 calm, 1 strong } ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/scene-sample.title: scene/sample
reference/scene-sample.text: scene/sample import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/scene/sample" Package sample builds a small made-up island that uses every feature the renderers draw: relief with snow, the sea with a tide, a river, instanced trees with levels of detail that sway, a house with stone, shingle and plank patterns, a paved square, a glowing lamp, a waterfall, an unlit flag, a glass box, the sky with clouds, moon and a constellation, and a label. It needs no files, so tests and backend comparisons can draw the same scene anywhere. Functions Function func Island() *scene.Scene Island returns the scene, with the sun in the afternoon. func Night() *scene.Scene Night returns the island an hour before midnight, under the moon and the stars. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/software.text: software import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/software" Package software is the beginning of a software backend for the immediate-mode Renderer contract. It will be built later: until then every function returns NotImplemented. Constants and variables var NotImplemented = failure.Define("software.not-implemented", "the software backend is not implemented yet") NotImplemented is what every function of the software backend returns until it is built. Renderer Renderer will draw the immediate-mode shapes (immediate.Renderer) with software. Until it is built, every method returns NotImplemented. type Renderer struct{} Function or method func (Renderer) RenderImage(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, bytes []byte, centre graphics.Vector, width float32, height float32, shader *string) error RenderImage returns NotImplemented. func (Renderer) RenderModel(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, model *immediate.Model, shader *string) error RenderModel returns NotImplemented. func (Renderer) RenderObject(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, vertices []graphics.Vector, shader *string) error RenderObject returns NotImplemented. func (Renderer) RenderPolygon(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, coordinates []graphics.Vector, shader *string, fill bool) error RenderPolygon returns NotImplemented. func (Renderer) RenderRectangle(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, centre graphics.Vector, width float32, height float32, shader *string, fill bool) error RenderRectangle returns NotImplemented. func (Renderer) RenderTriangle(space graphics.CoordinateSpace, coordinates []graphics.Vector, shader *string, fill bool) error RenderTriangle returns NotImplemented. func (Renderer) SetMatrices(projection, view, model graphics.Matrix) SetMatrices does nothing yet: it has no error to return. Until it is built, every method returns NotImplemented. type Window struct{} Function or method func (*Window) Draw(app *window.Application) error Draw returns NotImplemented. func (*Window) Run(app *window.Application) error Run returns NotImplemented. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/viewer.title: viewer
reference/viewer.text: viewer import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/viewer" Package viewer is an interactive explorer for a scene.Scene: orbit and walking cameras, sun, fog, shadows and vertical exaggeration controls, headless captures and benchmarks. Programs pass an optional update function, called at every fixed step, to change the scene while it is shown (a simulation, for example); the viewer itself knows nothing about what changes it. Controls: left drag rotates, right drag pans, scroll zooms (orbit camera). Tab switches to walking on the ground: WASD or arrows move, mouse looks, shift runs, [ and ] change the walking speed. J/L turn the sun, I/K raise or lower it (below the horizon it is night), N jumps between day and night, Z/X change the vertical exaggeration, F toggles fog, O toggles shadows. M switches to a map: the ground from straight above without perspective, then an isometric view, then back; on the map any drag moves it, scroll zooms and Q/E turn it a quarter. Functions Function func Edit(world *scene.Scene, options Options, title string, edit EditFunc) error Edit shows the scene like Run, for a program that edits it (a level editor, a floor plan designer). func Run(world *scene.Scene, options Options, title string, update UpdateFunc) error Run shows the scene until the window closes (or, for a capture or a benchmark, until it is done). Constants and variables var ( // InvalidPoint is a point flag (-look-at) not written as two numbers, "x,z". InvalidPoint = failure.Define("viewer.invalid-point", "a point is written as two numbers, x,z") // UnknownBackend is a -backend that is not automatic, metal or opengl. UnknownBackend = failure.Define("viewer.unknown-backend", "the backend is automatic, metal or opengl") ) Codes of the errors the viewer's flags return. Backend Backend is the graphics interface a session draws through. type Backend string const ( Automatic Backend = "" // Metal on macOS, falling back to OpenGL if it cannot start; OpenGL elsewhere Metal Backend = "metal" // only on macOS OpenGL Backend = "opengl" // OpenGL 4.1 ) Function or method func (backend *Backend) Set(text string) error Set reads a backend from a flag: automatic, metal or opengl. func (backend *Backend) String() string String is the backend as its flag writes it: automatic, metal or opengl. EditFunc EditFunc changes the scene in answer to the user, at every step the viewer runs, before the viewer's own controls; view tells where the camera that drew the last frame was, so the program can find what the pointer is on (View.PointOnPlane, View.PointOnGround). type EditFunc func(world *scene.Scene, state *input.State, step float64, view View) Measure Measure says what a session captures or measures instead of being explored. type Measure struct { // CapturePath renders one frame to this PNG (in a hidden window) instead of exploring. CapturePath string // BenchmarkFrames measures this many frames, writes their times to Output and ends; 0 // explores. BenchmarkFrames int // LoadingTime is how long the scene took to load, shown with the benchmark's times. LoadingTime time.Duration // Output is where a benchmark writes its report; nil writes it nowhere. Output io.Writer } Options Options configure a viewing session, in three groups: where the view starts, how it is drawn, and what is measured or captured. type Options struct { // Width and Height are the window's size. Width, Height int Start Start Rendering Rendering Measure Measure // Backend is what draws: Automatic (Metal on macOS, OpenGL elsewhere), Metal or OpenGL. Backend Backend } Function or method func DefaultOptions() Options DefaultOptions returns a 1280×800 window with the scene's own sun, reporting benchmarks on the standard output. func (options *Options) RegisterFlags(flags *flag.FlagSet) RegisterFlags declares the viewer options as command-line flags, starting from the defaults. Rendering Rendering are switches of how frames are drawn. type Rendering struct { NoShadows bool // NoVsync draws as fast as possible instead of waiting for the display. NoVsync bool // Continuous draws every frame, so water, clouds and plants in the wind keep moving while // nothing else happens. By default the viewer draws only when something changes (input, the // camera, the sun, notices), unless it runs a program's update function (a simulation). Continuous bool // FixedSeconds, when not NaN, draws every frame as if this many seconds had passed (water, // clouds and waterfalls stand still): captures that must come out the same, to compare them. FixedSeconds float64 } Start Start is where the view starts looking from, and the light it starts in. type Start struct { Walking bool // on the ground, walking Map bool // on the map: the ground from straight above, without perspective Isometric bool // on the map's isometric view Night bool // LookAt is the point (x, z) the view starts centred on, and where walking starts; nil is the // scene's centre. LookAt *[2]float32 // Zoom is the starting orbit distance (or map span) as a fraction of the default; 0 is 1. Zoom float64 // SunElevationDegrees and SunAzimuthDegrees (clockwise from north) place the sun; NaN keeps // the scene's. SunElevationDegrees float64 SunAzimuthDegrees float64 // HeadingDegrees, clockwise from north (-z), is the way the walker starts facing; NaN keeps // the default. PitchDegrees is how far it starts looking up (negative is down). HeadingDegrees float64 PitchDegrees float64 // EyeHeight (scene units) and WalkSpeed (scene units a second) of the walker; 0 keeps the // default, a share of the scene's size. EyeHeight float64 WalkSpeed float64 } UpdateFunc UpdateFunc changes the scene at every fixed step (seconds), before the viewer's own controls; state is the keyboard and mouse, for programs that add their own keys. type UpdateFunc func(world *scene.Scene, state *input.State, step float64) View View is what an editing program knows about the view at a step: the camera that drew the frame the user sees, and the window's size. The pointer's position (input.State.CursorX and CursorY) is in the same window pixels. type View struct { Camera camera.Lens Width, Height int // window pixels // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func (view View) FrameGround(minimumX, minimumZ, maximumX, maximumZ float32) FrameGround asks the cameras to show a rectangle of ground whole (x and z from minimum to maximum): they aim at its middle and the map's span fits it in the window. func (view View) PointOnGround(x, y float64) (graphics.Vector, bool) PointOnGround returns the point of the window (x, y in window pixels) on the scene's walkable ground (meshes marked Ground), with its true height. func (view View) PointOnPlane(x, y float64, height float32) (graphics.Vector, bool) PointOnPlane returns the point of the window (x, y in window pixels) on the horizontal plane at a true height: a flat floor. func (view View) Ray(x, y float64) (camera.Ray, bool) Ray returns the ray from the camera through a point of the window, in drawn heights. func (view View) Span() float64 Span is how much ground the map shows from the bottom of the window to its top, in world units: a program shows its zoom from it. func (view View) ZoomBy(factor float64) ZoomBy asks the cameras to come nearer by a factor (2 shows half as much, 0.5 twice as much), keeping what they aim at, as a zoom button does. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/window.title: window
reference/window.text: window import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/window" Package window describes a program that draws in a window: what the window is (Options), what the program does every frame (Callbacks) and what the two share while it runs (Application). A backend (opengl.Window, metal.Window, the Android and browser loops) opens the window and drives the application. Constants and variables const DefaultCapturePath = "frame.png" DefaultCapturePath is where a Headless application saves its frame when CapturePath is empty. Application Application is a program running in a window: its Options and Callbacks, and what the backend and the program share while it runs. type Application struct { Options Callbacks // Input, when not nil, is filled by the backend every frame (keyboard, mouse, touches, pads). Input *input.State // Renderer draws immediate-mode shapes; the backend fills it. Renderer immediate.Renderer // Camera is where the immediate-mode shapes are seen from. Camera camera.Lens // Stop, when set by Update or Draw, ends the application after the current frame. Stop bool // ModelMatrix, ViewMatrix and ProjectionMatrix are the immediate-mode matrices: the backend // sets the view and projection from Camera each frame, and the model matrix starts as the // identity. ModelMatrix graphics.Matrix ViewMatrix graphics.Matrix ProjectionMatrix graphics.Matrix } Backend Backend opens a window (or a hidden one, for a Headless application) and drives an Application in it: opengl.Window, metal.Window and the software, Vulkan and WebGPU stubs. type Backend interface { // Run opens the window and runs the application until it closes or sets Stop. Run(app *Application) error // Draw draws one frame of the application. Draw(app *Application) error } Callbacks Callbacks are what the program does every frame. Each may be nil. type Callbacks struct { // Update runs at a fixed time step (Options.FixedStepSeconds) before drawing: where // simulations and camera controllers advance. stepSeconds is always that step. Update func(app *Application, stepSeconds float64) error // Draw draws a frame. Draw func(app *Application) error // Unchanged, when set, is asked before each frame is drawn: true means the frame would look // exactly like the last one shown, and the backend skips drawing and presenting it. An // interface answers by comparing its draw list's fingerprint (draw2d.List.Fingerprint), so a // pointer moving over still parts of a window costs an update step and nothing more. Unchanged func(app *Application) bool } Kind Kind says whether a window is shown. type Kind int const ( // OnScreen is a window shown on the screen, the default. OnScreen Kind = iota // Headless draws one frame in a hidden window and saves it to Options.CapturePath. Headless ) Options Options are what the window is: chosen before it opens. type Options struct { Kind Kind // Title and Version are shown in the window's title bar. Title string Version string // Width and Height are the window's size in screen coordinates. Width int Height int // MinWidth and MinHeight, when above 0, stop the window from being made smaller. MinWidth, MinHeight int // Background is the colour (red, green, blue, alpha from 0 to 1) a frame is cleared to. Background graphics.Vector // FixedStepSeconds is the time step of Callbacks.Update; 0 is 1/60 of a second. FixedStepSeconds float64 // CapturePath is where a Headless application saves its frame (PNG); DefaultCapturePath // when empty. CapturePath string // DrawOnDemand draws only when something happens (input, a resize, a frame asked for with // Input.RequestFrame, or opengl.Wake from another goroutine) instead of every frame: the // program sleeps in between, which an interface that is mostly still needs for the battery. // Each frame runs exactly one update step. Needs Application.Input. DrawOnDemand bool // FlatOnly asks for a window with no depth or stencil buffer: a program that only draws flat // shapes (an interface, see opengl.FlatRenderer) saves a buffer the size of the window, about // 14 MB for a 1280 × 720 window on a high-density screen. It also skips the 3D renderer's // shaders and its part of each frame (the flat renderer clears and draws the whole window), and // on a Mac with two GPUs lets the system keep the window on the integrated, low-power one. FlatOnly bool // DisableVsync draws frames as fast as possible instead of waiting for the display (benchmarks). DisableVsync bool // ShowFramesPerSecond writes the frames drawn each second in the title, for a window that // draws every frame (not on demand). ShowFramesPerSecond bool } Function or method func (options Options) CapturePathOrDefault() string CapturePathOrDefault returns where a Headless application saves its frame. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

reference/windowloop.text: windowloop import "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/windowloop" Package windowloop runs a GLFW window's main loop for any drawing backend (OpenGL, Metal): the window's events, input, drawing on demand, the fixed-step update clock, frames asked for while the window is being resized, the pointer's shape and lock, and the whole screen. A backend only has to draw and show a frame. Functions Function func ApplyCursorLock(window *glfw.Window, state *input.State, currentlyLocked *bool) ApplyCursorLock captures or releases the cursor when the application changes its request. func ForwardInput(window *glfw.Window, state *input.State) ForwardInput sends GLFW keyboard, mouse, scroll and text events into an input.State, and gives it the system clipboard. func OnMainThread() bool OnMainThread is only checked on macOS, the one system that requires it. func Run(glfwWindow *glfw.Window, app *window.Application, clock *frameloop.Clock, drawFrame func() error) error Run calls the application's update steps and drawFrame until the window closes or the application stops. func UpdateSizes(window *glfw.Window, state *input.State) UpdateSizes copies the framebuffer and window sizes into the input state. func Wake() Wake makes a window that draws on demand draw a frame now: for a program whose data changes on another goroutine (a download finishing, a message arriving). Constants and variables var NotOnMainThread = failure.Define("windowloop.not-on-main-thread", CursorShapes CursorShapes shows the pointer shape the application asks for, creating each system cursor once. type CursorShapes struct { // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func (shapes *CursorShapes) Apply(window *glfw.Window, state *input.State) Apply shows the pointer shape the state asks for, if it is not already shown.
